symptoms.description: The racket head does not flip back or flips much slower without explosive lag.
The swing feels dead and lacks effortless release on stationary or inside-out forehands compared to running forehands.
The forehand slot feels restricted rather than loose and comfortable.

causes.statement: The player initiates the forward swing with a swing vector directed toward the ball rather than laterally outward to the side.
The player attempts to flip the racket tip backward while keeping the hand still, rotating around the butt cap rather than moving head and hand equal and opposite around the center of mass.
The player sets up too close to the ball laterally, causing the brain to inhibit outward hand motion to avoid missing the shot.
When stationary or moving inside-out, the player fails to actively press the hand outward against the body's natural leftward momentum.

angles.summary: Moving the hand outward while the racket head flips backward spins the frame closer to its center of mass, making it flip twice as fast.
Pro players direct their hand horizontally outward to the right for the majority of the forward swing, turning toward the target only right at contact.
Flipping around the butt cap with a still hand produces a slow, casual flick rather than maximum explosive lag and release.
Pressing the hand outward creates a slot that feels loose and comfortable rather than forced.
Jack Sock presses the racket out earlier and wider than anyone else, maximizing wrist extension and power.

solutions.summary: Create significantly more lateral space in the left-to-right direction during setup than feels necessary.
solutions.external_goal: Leave abundant horizontal lateral distance between yourself and the ball path.

solutions.summary: Throw your hitting hand horizontally outward to the right to start the forward swing.
solutions.external_goal: Direct the hand toward the right sideline at swing initiation rather than toward the opponent.

solutions.summary: Actively press the hand outward to the right to overcome body momentum when stationary or moving inside-out.
solutions.external_goal: Press the hand outward to the right against the body's leftward drift.

solutions.summary: Use a kinesthetic cue to press the racket and hand outward early to guarantee the flip occurs.
solutions.external_goal: Press the racket out early to the right before initiating forward drive.
